paper_style.palette_strategy: Pastel module bands and boxes structure the pipeline; red text marks matched-condition best table values; Figure 7 uses gray versus coral for initial versus generated keywords. Natural-image montages carry content colors rather than semantic category colors.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: Figures 1 and 4–6 mix vector diagrams/arrows/text with JPEG thumbnails; Figures 2–3 mix JPEG panels with vector labels/separators; Figure 7 and all tables are predominantly vector.
paper_style.style_consistency: Caption placement and numbering are consistent, metric headers/arrows recur across quantitative tables, and diagram pastel vocabulary is reused across Figures 1 and 4–6; image montages and Figure 7 form separate visual subsystems.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: Framework Overview: PRISM generates structured text descriptions for each training image using a VLM to iteratively extract brain-aligned object attributes and relationships. These descriptions capture the image’s compositional and relational content and serve as supervision to train an encoder and fine-tune a language model to map fMRI signals into the text space. During inference, the model predicts descriptions from fMRI signals, which then guide a pre-trained diffusion model for object-centric image reconstruction.

encodings.shape: rectangular modules, arrows and object blocks encode stages
encodings.line: solid arrows and dashed training/inference separators
encodings.text: direct labels for modules, conditions, objects and outputs

figures.data_and_statistics: Non-numeric workflow: VLM/search creates structured descriptions, fMRI-to-text projects to text, two object conditions use cross-attention and latent concatenation, then generate the reconstructed image.
figures.evidence_relation: §3.1 latent-space motivation → Figure 1 method interface → §3.2–§3.3 structured description and object-centric generation; Tables 1 and 5 test the represented choices, Figures 4–6 instantiate the object branches.
design_strengths: Training and inference are closed in one traceable pipeline.
Panel bands, arrows, text boxes and dashed boundaries redundantly encode module roles.
Structured object examples connect the text bridge to later ablations.
design_weaknesses: Top search loop and two-condition bottom block are dense and some labels are small.
The distinction between text and structured description, CKA/LPIPS objective and m=2 constraint is not quantitatively encoded.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use training/inference partitions, module color bands, object branches and a merge node to make an input-to-output mechanism traceable; label branch conditions directly.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Table 1 establishes LM text alignment; Figure 1 turns it into structured-description and object-centric-generation interfaces; Tables 2–3 provide headline and semantic-QA results; Figure 2 supplies aligned qualitative rows; Tables 4–5 test latent choice and module necessity; Appendix Figures 3–6 and Tables 7–9 expose failure, object-count, cross-dataset and search boundaries, while Figure 7 expands keyword search to all candidates.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Captions use Figure/Table n prefixes, put Table captions above tables and Figure captions below figures, and often define metric directions and red best highlighting. Figure 1 is most self-contained; Figures 4–6 and Table 9 are title-only/near-title-only, and ± notation, sampling and aggregation often remain in prose.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: PixCorr, SSIM, LPIPS, CLIP and Inception V3 with ↑/↓ recur across Tables 2, 4, 5, 7 and 8; rank×round keyword headers recur in Tables 6 and 9. Table 2 adds dataset groups/backbone conditions, and Table 3 defines method abbreviations in its caption.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 1 text latent and object-wise cross-attention map to Table 1 alignment, Table 4 latent reconstruction and Table 5 module deletion. Figures 4–6 illustrate branches evaluated by Tables 5 and 8, while Table 3 QA is adjacent to but statistically separate from Figure 2.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Main Table 4 points to Appendix Table 7; main Table 6 is expanded by Figure 7 and stress-tested by Table 9; Figure 1 object-centric blocks are instantiated by Figures 3–6 and constrained by Table 8. Appendix I–K preserve prompt parameters/prompts but not seeds or participant count.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Georgia/Nimbus Roman dominates captions, tables and diagram labels; Computer Modern/CambriaMath handles equations; NimbusMonL is used for keyword table entries. PDF font objects are mixed and small sizes are estimated.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Pastel module colors and red best-value highlighting are coherent across method and quantitative subsystems, but natural image colors are not semantic encodings and Figure 7 gray/coral key is not grayscale-safe.

most_reusable_patterns: Figure 1 training/inference partition, module bands, object branches and merge node make an intermediate-representation pipeline traceable.
Isomorphic latent/module/object-count tables (Tables 4, 5, 7, 8) preserve metric columns for direct mechanism and cross-dataset comparison.
Table 6 rank×round summary, Figure 7 full distribution and Table 9 seed-exclusion trajectory layer evidence for black-box prompt search.
Figure 3 fixes attribute-binding failure semantics before Figures 4–6 show object-level decomposition.
highest_value_objects: Figure 1 — method interface and causal overview.
Table 1 plus Table 4 — representation choice from alignment to reconstruction consequence.
Table 5 — module necessity under deletion/fixed-prompt controls.
failure_patterns: Table 3’s “significantly” claim has no displayed test, uncertainty or sample aggregation.
Figure 2 and Figures 3–6 are selected qualitative cases without sampling rule, seed context or systematic failure rate.
Tables 2, 4, 5, 7 and 8 print ± without a consistent local definition; Table 8 also mixes precision.
Fixed m=2 slots and predefined positions are a boundary; more object-level features can omit objects.
Prompt search uses 667 sampled NSD training images, SDXL coverage is limited to PRISM/Mindeye2, and Figure 7 is dense/color-dependent.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: The paper uses a latent-alignment-to-structured-object-generation pipeline, isomorphic metric tables and appendix failure/search cases to present PRISM’s mechanism and performance, but local uncertainty definitions, QA testing and qualitative sampling rules remain incomplete.
